title: Condensed Narrative Mode + Hybrid Rendering for High-Density Time-series
creator: Aisha Khan
summary: Add a new 'Condensed Narrative' accessibility mode for time-series charts that generates lightweight human-readable summaries for screen readers, paired with a hybrid rendering strategy (canvas decimation + SVG focus overlays) to improve interactive perf on very large series.
description:
Problem:
- High-density time-series (50k+ points) create heavy DOM and long paint times. Screen reader users get no concise context (raw axis values and long tables are noisy).
- We need a pattern in the design system that: 1) provides accessible, human-focused summaries of trends/anomalies; 2) reduces DOM/ARIA verbosity; 3) keeps interactive pan/zoom and tooltip fidelity for sighted users; 4) degrades gracefully on low-power devices.

Proposal:
- Condensed Narrative Mode (CNM): an optional chart mode that exposes a single accessible summary block per chart containing a short natural-language description (3-5 sentences) describing the dominant trend, latest value delta, detected anomalies (count + timestamps), and recommended follow-ups. The block is the primary screen-reader target (aria-live polite) instead of exposing every data point.
- Narrative templates: small, testable templates that cover monotonic trends, seasonal patterns, spikes/plateaus, and flatness. Maintain a templating spec in docs for consistency across charts.
- Hybrid Rendering Strategy: default visible layer uses decimated canvas drawing for the full series (fast paint, minimal DOM). An overlay SVG layer renders focus elements (selection handles, legend markers, hover lines) for crisp interaction and accessibility hooks (ARIA roles on handles, not on thousands of points).
- Keyboard / Focus model: keyboard focus lands on chart container -> control menu -> condensed narrative -> press Enter to toggle focus to interactive overlay (small number of interactive elements only).
- Energy and low-power mode: auto-enable more aggressive decimation on devices reporting reduced power mode or when battery low to preserve responsiveness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accessibility:
  - Screen reader reads condensed narrative within 300ms of chart render with aria-live polite.
  - Narrative covers: overall direction (rise/fall/flat), percent change over visible window, up to 3 anomalies with timestamps, and a short CTA if applicable.
  - Keyboard traversal: chart container -> narrative -> overlay elements. Verified in VoiceOver (Mac), NVDA (Windows), TalkBack (Android web).
- Performance:
  - For a 100k-point series, initial render <= 150ms on a mid-range laptop (cold load) and pan/zoom frame updates <= 80ms for typical viewport changes.
  - DOM node reduction: at least 90% fewer interactive DOM nodes vs naive per-point SVG rendering for large series.
- Visual parity:
  - Hover/tooltip content for focused points must match existing tooltip copy and accept the same structured output schema.
- Rollout / Feature flagging:
  - Implementation behind flag `chart.condensedNarrative` and `chart.hybridRendering` for staged rollout.

Design deliverables:
- Figma spec with narrative templates + examples for 5 series archetypes (monotonic rise, cyclical, noisy with spikes, plateau then drop, sparse with outliers). Link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/condensed-narrative-charts (mock).
- Component API surface (design): Chart props: {mode: 'default'|'condensedNarrative', narrativeTemplates: string[], decimationStrategy: 'largest-triangle'|'reservoir', lowPowerThreshold: number}. (Will be turned into a small prop spec doc for engineers.)

Engineering notes / constraints:
- Backend: algorithm to produce narrative must run client-side using precomputed summary stats (min/max/mean/median/percentile/spike-count) passed down by telemetry or computed from visible window. Avoid O(n) work on main thread for huge series—use WebWorker for full recompute or incremental summaries from server.
- Graphics: use an offscreen canvas where available and CompositeLayers pattern to composite canvas + SVG overlays.
- Metrics: emit telemetry events when CNM is used, and capture perceived latency via RUM.

QA checklist:
- Manual a11y test on VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack for each archetype.
- Automated axe-core smoke tests for the chart container and narrative block.
- Performance bench: synthetic harness to replay 100k points and measure TTFP and p95 interaction latency.

Dependencies:
- ENG-71240 (rendering kernel upgrades for offscreen canvas)
- ENG-70512 (telemetry: series summaries endpoint)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Narrative template may oversimplify and hide edge cases. Mitigation: provide a verbatim 'data inspector' button that opens raw values for power users and persists in UI for analysts.
- Risk: Over-aggressive decimation loses important spikes. Mitigation: anomaly-preserving decimation (keep top-k largest residuals) and surfacing flagged timestamps in narrative.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Internal dogfood behind flags for design/eng (10% of org).
- Phase 2: Beta group (customers who opt in) with telemetry tracking for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3: Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% if error and regressions are acceptable.
